title: Intracortical speech neuroprosthesis restores conversation for a man with ALS (UC Davis, BrainGate2)
summary: Four 64-electrode arrays plus RNN decoder let Casey Harrell (ALS) converse at 97.5% accuracy; later 1.96 million words at home
account: At the University of California Davis, a 45-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and severe dysarthria took part in the BrainGate2 trial (NCT00912041). Press identify him as Casey Harrell. Four 64-electrode arrays were implanted in his left precentral gyrus in July 2023. From August 2023, a decoder predicting phonemes every 80 ms, with language models over a 125,000-word vocabulary, converted his attempted speech to text. Accuracy was 99.6% with a 50-word vocabulary on day one and 90.2% with the full vocabulary on day two. It was 97.5% sustained over 248 hours of self-paced conversation with family, friends and colleagues (Card et al., NEJM, August 2024). The paper gives only the month for the first session, so 1 August 2023 is used.
purpose: Built to restore communication by decoding attempted speech from intracortical activity into text. Conversational communication was the intended benefit and is what occurred.
system: UC Davis intracortical speech neuroprosthesis (BrainGate2 trial)
model_version: Four 64-electrode microelectrode arrays (256 electrodes) in the left precentral gyrus; phoneme decoder with an openly available language model assembling phonemes into words and two further open-source language models producing the sentence, over a 125,000-word vocabulary
developer: UC Davis Neuroprosthetics Lab (Brandman, Stavisky) with the BrainGate consortium

ratings.reason: Life-changing benefit to one identifiable person: conversational communication with family and colleagues was restored. The 2026 follow-up documents over 3,800 hours of unsupervised home use, nearly two million words and continued full-time employment.

ai_role.statement: A neural-network decoder (phoneme prediction every 80 ms) combined with language models is the mechanism converting attempted speech into text. The benefit is attributable to the decoding system, with surgery and arrays as enabling hardware.

fields.account: At the University of California Davis, a 45-year-old man with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis and severe dysarthria took part in the BrainGate2 trial (NCT00912041). Press identify him as Casey Harrell. Four 64-electrode arrays were implanted in his left precentral gyrus in July 2023. From August 2023, a decoder predicting phonemes every 80 ms, with language models over a 125,000-word vocabulary, converted his attempted speech to text. Accuracy was 99.6% with a 50-word vocabulary on day one and 90.2% with the full vocabulary on day two. It was 97.5% sustained over 248 hours of self-paced conversation with family, friends and colleagues (Card et al., NEJM, August 2024). The paper gives only the month for the first session, so 1 August 2023 is used.

echoes.setting: Same participant, at-home independent use over nearly two years: 183,060 sentences, 1,960,163 words, 56 words per minute, full-time employment maintained
echoes.source: Card NS, et al. (2026). Long-term independent use of an intracortical brain-computer interface for speech and cursor control. Nature Medicine. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13375540/

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.
